BITCOIN MINING INSIGHTS

Plain-language guides on halving, difficulty and mining in Oman. Updated 20 Nov 2026. Educational only, not financial advice.

NEXT BITCOIN HALVING (BLOCK 1,050,000)
Loading…
HALVING · 5 min read

What the Bitcoin halving means for miners

Every 210,000 blocks (about four years) the reward paid for each new block is cut in half. The April 2024 halving took it from 6.25 to 3.125 BTC, and the next one, at block 1,050,000, will take it to 1.5625 BTC.

For a miner, a halving cuts income per block in coin terms overnight. If the price does not rise enough to make up for it, only efficient machines and cheap power stay profitable. That is why joules per terahash (J/TH) and electricity cost matter more after every halving.

Test your own numbers in the profit calculator.

DIFFICULTY · 4 min read

Mining difficulty explained

The network adjusts difficulty every 2,016 blocks (roughly two weeks) so that a block is found about every ten minutes. When more hashrate joins, difficulty rises and each machine earns a smaller share of the same rewards. When miners leave, it falls.

Difficulty changes are normal and expected. What matters is the trend: rising difficulty with a flat price squeezes margins. Plan with a buffer for difficulty growth rather than today's figures alone.

Current network hashrate: …. See how it affects earnings in the calculator.

OMAN · 6 min read

Bitcoin mining in Oman: what to check first

Four things decide whether a site works: the electricity tariff and grid capacity, the climate and cooling method, the connection and security setup, and the regulatory position.

Oman's summer heat makes cooling a major cost. Liquid (hydro) cooling and good airflow design keep machines stable and can raise uptime and hashrate. Hosting with an operator avoids building your own site, but you should still check the contract, power price, SLA and fees.

Rules for mining and digital assets can change. Confirm the current position with the relevant Omani authorities and a qualified adviser before you commit. See our hosting packages or ask us.
